title: Decide often, fail small
header_line: My analysis of one book on neuro-linguistic programming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: How many failures does it take for your ego to knock?
I said that you can make a decision and interpret things in your favor, you can be comfortable being uncomfortable, and comfortable adapting continually.
I said that from a probability standpoint, if you are making decisions all the time, even wrong ones, you will eventually make the right one and you will learn.

I described two mindsets in a business owner: one that wants to grow, take risks and decide, and another that has not felt the power to decide because of the responsibility of being the custodian of the business.
I said that there is no need for shame: it is only feedback, only adjustments. I asked how long it takes before your ego knocks on the door: three failures, four, seven?

I said that the first part is identifying how you manage your thoughts, then identifying other people's thoughts and limiting beliefs, and then more. I said happiness is discipline: you have the choice to wake up and call it the most extraordinary day.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a decision you are putting off.
Write the smallest version you can decide today.
Write how you will treat a wrong decision as feedback.
Write how many failures it takes for your ego to knock.
Write the discipline you will start with.

check.q: What did I say a wrong decision is?
What did I say happens if you decide all the time?
choices: You eventually decide right and learn

check.q: What did I say happiness is?

recap: Decide often. Treat mistakes as feedback. Keep the discipline.
